title: Subjectivity Before Personal Identity: A Missing Foundation in the Debate on Transhumanism
description: Argues that the debate on mind uploading — including Ralph Weir's influential critique of transhumanism — presupposes that a digital system can be a subject, without establishing the conditions under which this holds. Submitted to Minds and Machines.

title: A Foundation for Transhumanism
description: The second part of the Causa Sui project: transhumanism formulated a goal — the expansion of the space of reachable states — but never a rigorous mechanism for reaching it. This part supplies one.

title: Project Causa Sui
description: A working theory of subjecthood: genuine subjectivity — responsibility, fear, creativity — arises from the irreversibility of a substrate's state, not from computational complexity.
